findings.quoted_text: These manufacturing services shall include, but not be limited to, labor, materials, testing, packaging and delivery to Customer, all subject to the terms and conditions contained in this Agreement.
Contractor and Customer agree to terms of payments of current plus thirty (30) days from the date of invoice.

Contractor shall defend, indemnify and hold harmless Customer from all claims, liabilities, costs, damages, judgments and attorney's fees resulting from or arising out of any alleged and/or actual infringement or other violation of any patents, patent rights, trademarks, trademark rights, trade names, trade name rights, copyrights, trade secrets, proprietary rights and processes or other such rights as a result of the manufacturing methods employed by Contractor
These manufacturing services shall include, but not be limited to, labor, materials, testing, packaging and delivery to Customer, all subject to the terms and conditions contained in this Agreement.
findings.explanation: The open-ended phrasing "shall include, but not be limited to" creates ambiguity in the scope of work, potentially enabling the Customer to demand extra tasks without adjusting compensation.
findings.suggested_change: Replace "shall include, but not be limited to" with a definitive list of services and state that any additional services require a mutually agreed change order.

findings.quoted_text: Contractor and Customer agree to terms of payments of current plus thirty (30) days from the date of invoice.
findings.explanation: Net 30 payment terms mean the Contractor must finance material procurement, labor, and production costs for over a month after invoicing before receiving funds.
findings.suggested_change: Propose shorter payment terms, such as Net 15, or implement milestone and advance payments for material costs.

findings.quoted_text: Contractor shall defend, indemnify and hold harmless Customer from all claims, liabilities, costs, damages, judgments and attorney's fees resulting from or arising out of any alleged and/or actual infringement or other violation of any patents, patent rights, trademarks, trademark rights, trade names, trade name rights, copyrights, trade secrets, proprietary rights and processes or other such rights as a result of the manufacturing methods employed by Contractor
findings.explanation: Indemnifying the Customer against third-party IP claims related to manufacturing methods can expose the Contractor to substantial financial liability if not strictly limited.
findings.suggested_change: Explicitly limit and cap the Contractor's indemnification obligations under this section to align with the overall limitation of liability.

content.subject: Proposed changes to the agreement
content.body: Hello, I have reviewed the agreement and would like to propose a few adjustments before signing. - Regarding the relevant clause on manufacturing services, the open-ended phrasing creates ambiguity in the scope of work; please replace this with a definitive list of services and state that any additional services require a mutually agreed change order. - Regarding the relevant clause on payment terms, current plus thirty days creates a delay in receiving funds; please propose shorter payment terms, such as Net 15, or implement milestone and advance payments for material costs. - Regarding the relevant clause on indemnification, the current wording creates substantial financial exposure; please explicitly limit and cap the indemnification obligations under this section to align with the overall limitation of liability. Thank you for your time and best regards,
